title: Power Supply State Changes
exclusions: Detects a transition between two adjacent, complete, normalized snapshots for the same physical server power-supply unit and the same authoritative collector contract. It does not alert merely because a current state is non-healthy, replay IPMI System Event Log history, infer an unobserved transition across a gap longer than 15 minutes, or compare Redfish and IPMI observations as if they were one continuous series. It does not measure voltage, current, watts, efficiency, energy, UPS or rack-PDU state, utility quality, battery runtime, thermal state, host power-on state, or operating-system availability; discover a PSU that never entered inventory; prove that a reported fault is physically real; validate firmware interpretation; decode unqualified OEM states; establish root cause or adversary intent; secure the BMC; or perform power, failover, acknowledgement, reset, or remediation actions. Collection errors, stale targets, duplicate samples, unknown values, unsupported facets, identity churn, and incomplete inventory require separate source-health controls. This operational monitor makes no regulatory or MITRE ATT&CK coverage claim.
evidence: After deployment, retain the versioned `power_supply_state_changes` saved-search definition, ACL and schedule; the effective `TA_power_supply_state` input and JSON extraction configuration; reviewed collector/adapter hash; contract and mapping-table revision; BMC, chassis, PSU-slot and collector inventory; Redfish service/schema or IPMI tool and BMC firmware versions used during qualification; adjacent raw snapshots for each finding; scheduler and alert-action records; exact suppression decision; and dated positive and negative control output. Each finding must preserve host, stable BMC and PSU identities, source protocol, sample epochs, interval, changed facets, previous/current canonical states, raw native state evidence, severity, and transition direction. A same-time read from the BMC hardware-health page and a fresh Redfish resource or qualified IPMI sensor/FRU read is corroborating evidence. These artifacts show what the management controller and normalization contract reported; this documentation-only review produced no runtime evidence and did not certify a PSU, collector, BMC, or Splunk deployment.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated test index, ingest three schema-1 `source=power_supply_state_snapshot sourcetype=hardware:power_supply:state` events for `host=psu-positive`, `bmc_id=bmc-01`, `collector_instance=dc1-bmc-poller`, `source_protocol=redfish`, and `psu_id=chassis-1:bay-1`, spaced 300 seconds apart inside fixed search bounds. Every event has `collector_status=ok`, `snapshot_complete=1`, and all canonical facets populated. Event 1 is `present/enabled/ok/normal/clear/clear/ok/full`; event 2 changes `health_state` to `warning` and `redundancy_state` to `degraded`; event 3 restores both to `ok/full`. Run the catalogue SPL with the index, base time range, and final `sample_epoch` result bounds changed to absolute fixture bounds. Expect exactly two rows: a high, degraded transition whose `changed_fields` contains both facets and whose previous/current ranks are 0/3, followed by an info, recovered transition with ranks 3/0. Repeat with an IPMI sequence whose second snapshot changes `failure_state=failed` and `input_state=lost`; expect a critical degraded row without relying on message substrings.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Under the same fixed bounds, require zero findings independently for: one first-seen healthy sample; two identical complete samples; two samples whose native wording changes while all canonical facets remain equal; a `collector_status=request_error` event; `snapshot_complete=0`; a facet value of `unknown`; a transition only from `unsupported` to a supported value; adjacent samples 901 seconds apart; the same PSU observed once by Redfish and once by IPMI; a changed `collector_instance` or `contract_version`; and two events with the same exact sample identity, which must be rejected as a duplicate rather than ordered arbitrarily. Also create a real healthy-to-failed pair for a different `psu_id` and confirm it cannot supply the previous state for the tested unit. Verify the independent source-health search, not this transition search, reports errors, stale inventory, duplicates, unknown/unsupported drift, and missing expected PSUs.

dataSources: One complete normalized JSON event per inventoried power-supply slot every 300 seconds in deployment-local `index=hardware`, `source=power_supply_state_snapshot`, and `sourcetype=hardware:power_supply:state`. The preferred out-of-band adapter follows Redfish hyperlinks from `/redfish/v1/` through each Chassis `PowerSubsystem`, its `PowerSupplies` collection, individual `PowerSupply` resources, and `PowerSupplyRedundancy`, preserving `Status.State`, `Status.Health`, and standard `LineInputStatus`; qualify the deprecated chassis `Power` representation separately when it is the only vendor implementation. A separately qualified IPMI adapter polls current power-supply discrete sensor state and FRU/SDR identity; SEL entries are optional corroboration, not snapshots. Both adapters emit the same schema-1 identity, completeness, canonical-state, native-state, and sample-time contract. No standard Splunk add-on supplies this normalized transition contract.
app: A customer-managed `TA_power_supply_state` collection app containing one reviewed Redfish or IPMI adapter, a five-minute scheduled/modular or scripted input, strict normalization maps, JSON source-type configuration, inventory/source-health searches, and the saved search/dashboard knowledge objects. Use a least-privilege read-only Redfish account with a protected session-token workflow, or a separately approved IPMI read-only path. Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux is optional only for adjacent host context and is not a source for the power-supply snapshot fields queried here. No Splunk premium app or Splunkbase add-on is required.

description: Reports a server power-supply unit when one or more comparable canonical state facets differ between two adjacent, complete snapshots from the same Redfish or IPMI collector series. It preserves presence, operation, health, input, failure, predictive-failure, configuration, and redundancy transitions separately; rejects first sightings, duplicates, unknowns, unsupported-only changes, stale pairs, and cross-protocol comparisons; and labels degradation, recovery, and same-rank change without searching free-text fault words.
value: A redundant server can continue serving while one supply is absent, loses input, predicts failure, enters a vendor fault state, or leaves a redundancy set. Precise transition evidence gives hardware and data-center teams the affected chassis and bay, prior and current states, direction, and timing needed to respond before the remaining feed or supply fails, while also recording recovery and avoiding repeated alerts on a static fault, stale SEL message, collector restart, or harmless native-label change.
implementation: Deploy one authoritative read-only Redfish or IPMI adapter per managed PSU population in `TA_power_supply_state`, poll complete current state every five minutes, and emit the documented schema-1 JSON event for every inventoried slot. Preserve stable BMC, chassis, PSU, collector, and protocol identity; map only qualified native properties or current IPMI assertion bits into the closed canonical facets; use `unsupported` only when a facet is genuinely unavailable and `unknown` only in source-health events that cannot enter the transition search. Save the SPL as `power_supply_state_changes`, schedule it every five minutes over a delayed closed window, trigger on returned rows, and operate independent inventory, freshness, error, duplicate, and contract-drift controls. Validate degradation, recovery, unchanged, gap, duplicate, cross-source, and first-sample cases before notification routing.
visualization: Use a current-transition table with host, BMC, chassis, PSU ID/name, protocol, changed facets, previous/current values, direction, severity, sample interval, and native evidence. Add a 24-hour per-PSU state timeline that shows every canonical facet without coercing strings to numeric averages; tiles for critical degradations, recoveries, degraded or lost redundancy, stale BMCs, collection errors, duplicate samples, unknown facets, and expected-versus-observed PSU slots; and drilldowns to adjacent raw snapshots and the BMC inventory page. Keep current-state and transition panels separate: an old static critical state needs a current-health response but is not a new transition. Never label a Redfish `Health=Warning`, IPMI interpreted state, or redundancy loss as proof that the physical PSU is irreparable.
dataModelAcceleration: No documented Splunk Common Information Model dataset preserves BMC, chassis and PSU-slot identity; Redfish/IPMI source protocol; complete discrete state facets; snapshot completeness; adjacent sample epochs; native assertions; or redundancy-group state. Use the normalized raw-event contract. No accelerated `tstats` equivalent is claimed, and generic Change or Inventory events are not semantically interchangeable with a complete PSU state snapshot.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a real change under the qualified normalization contract. "False positive" here means the change was expected, mapped incorrectly, attached to the wrong physical identity, or not actionable under local policy.

1. **Approved hot-swap or redundancy test** — Pulling input, removing a supply, exercising failover, or replacing a FRU deliberately changes presence, input, failure, and redundancy facets. Confirm the exact chassis, bay, test owner, method, ticket, safety approval, and bounded UTC window. Preserve both degradation and recovery as control evidence even when notification is suppressed.

2. **BMC or system firmware maintenance** — A controller restart or firmware update can briefly report `Disabled`, `Absent`, degraded health, or incomplete redundancy while inventory rebuilds. A complete value can still be real from the API's perspective. Correlate reset/update records, adjacent snapshots, BMC uptime, and current hardware UI; do not globally suppress every PSU on the host.

3. **Platform initialization or orderly chassis power transition** — Some systems mark a supply standby, inactive, or disabled during POST, shutdown, cold start, or power-domain reconfiguration. Decide whether the transition is expected for that model and power policy. The rule records same-rank changes intentionally because operational-state movement can matter even when health remains OK.

4. **Native-to-canonical mapping defect** — OEM Redfish values, older embedded `Power` payloads, localized IPMI text, or a changed tool format can be mapped to the wrong facet. Compare raw resource URI/properties or sensor assertion bits with the mapping revision and vendor UI. Fix and requalify the adapter; do not add fault words to the SPL.

5. **PSU identity changed after service or firmware** — Redfish member URIs, array order, IPMI SDR record IDs, names, and FRU records can change. If `psu_id` is derived from a transient position, two physical units may be joined or one unit may appear new. Reconcile chassis and physical-location properties, slot labels, serial/part data, SDR/FRU identity, and inventory before suppression.

6. **Redundancy-group interpretation differs by platform** — A vendor can report a group warning during load sharing, capacity policy, or membership reconfiguration even when every member health is OK. Preserve the group's native mode, minimum-needed count, member links, and current status. Qualify the map for the exact model rather than treating member count alone as redundancy health.

7. **Duplicate authoritative collectors or delayed replay** — Two pollers using the same stable `collector_instance`, or replayed queue data with the same epoch, produce a rejected duplicate. Different collector IDs or protocols deliberately form separate series and therefore do not produce a transition. Resolve ownership and inventory; never merge sources by dropping protocol or collector identity.

8. **Input feed or environmental maintenance** — Utility transfer, branch-circuit work, rack PDU maintenance, or an approved single-feed operation can make `input_state=lost` or redundancy degraded while the PSU itself is functional. This is still an operationally real loss of resilience and should be correlated with facilities change records rather than relabeled healthy.

**Safe suppression:** keep the catalogue SPL unchanged and apply a post-result lookup such as `power_supply_state_exceptions.csv` only in the deployed notification wrapper. Key it on exact `host`, `bmc_id`, `chassis_id`, `psu_id`, `use_case`, and optionally `transition_direction`; require numeric `valid_from_epoch` and `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, and reason; reject wildcards, duplicate keys, open-ended rows, and expired bounds. Preserve suppressed transition rows in a review panel. Never suppress collector errors, stale/missing inventory, duplicate samples, unknown-state drift, all PSUs on a site, or a critical degradation merely because a warning transition was expected.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational server power-supply state-transition monitoring; no adversary behavior or intent is asserted)

cost.search_load_notes: Five-minute compact state snapshots, normally one event per inventoried PSU slot, and a short raw-event search that sorts each exact collector/protocol/PSU series and compares one prior complete sample.
sources: five-minute normalized Redfish or IPMI PSU snapshots

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and discrete-state contract

Assign a hardware-platform owner, facilities escalation owner, BMC access owner, Splunk collection owner, normalization-map owner, and alert-response owner. Inventory each BMC, chassis, physical PSU bay, expected member, redundancy group, management protocol, firmware, and service runbook before enabling notification. Use one authoritative adapter per PSU population. A second collector may be retained for corroboration, but it must have a different `collector_instance` or `source_protocol` and must not be merged into the transition series.

Grant only read access to inventory, PowerSupply/PowerSubsystem resources, current sensors, and FRU/SDR identity. A Redfish session account must not receive ConfigureManager, firmware-update, virtual-media, remote-console, or reset/power privileges merely to poll status. Validate the BMC TLS chain against a managed trust store; do not deploy permanent `curl -k` or disabled certificate verification. Keep credentials and session tokens in an approved secret mechanism and out of command lines, JSON, logs, checkpoints, and Splunk events. For IPMI, prefer a local in-band read path or an approved encrypted remote design with minimum privilege; never grant chassis control to the collector.

This UC compares complete current snapshots, not messages. A Redfish event subscription, BMC syslog message, or IPMI SEL record says that an event was recorded; it does not necessarily give the complete current state, can be replayed after forwarding interruption, and may persist after recovery. Use those feeds to corroborate timing only. Every successful poll emits one event per inventoried slot, including an absent slot when the platform represents it. `snapshot_complete=1` means identity and every canonical facet are populated with an allowed value; it does not mean healthy.

The closed schema-1 facets are `presence_state` (`present`, `absent`, `unsupported`), `operational_state` (`enabled`, `standby`, `disabled`, `offline`, `absent`, `unsupported`), `health_state` (`ok`, `warning`, `critical`, `unsupported`), `input_state` (`normal`, `lost`, `out_of_range`, `unsupported`), `failure_state` (`clear`, `failed`, `unsupported`), `predictive_failure` (`clear`, `asserted`, `unsupported`), `configuration_state` (`ok`, `mismatch`, `unsupported`), and `redundancy_state` (`full`, `degraded`, `lost`, `not_redundant`, `unsupported`). `unsupported` is a stable capability statement, not a synonym for healthy or missing. Emit `unknown` only with `snapshot_complete=0`; the primary SPL rejects it. Never turn a null, request failure, missing member, parser exception, stale cache, or unrecognized OEM value into `ok`, `clear`, or `absent`.

## Step 1 — Qualify Redfish or IPMI collection

For Redfish, start with `GET /redfish/v1/`, follow returned hyperlinks to the Chassis collection, then each chassis `PowerSubsystem`, the linked `PowerSupplies` collection, each member `@odata.id`, and `PowerSupplyRedundancy`. Do not manufacture a fixed chassis ID or member path. Current DMTF PowerSupply resources expose `Status.State` and `Status.Health`; the schema explicitly permits a slot resource whose State is `Absent`. Preserve `@odata.id`, `@odata.type`, `Id`, `Name`, Status values, physical location/part/serial fields when exposed, and the containing chassis identity as native evidence. Preserve redundancy member links, mode/type, minimum-needed information, and Status from the PowerSubsystem. If a platform only exposes the deprecated chassis `Power` resource with embedded `PowerSupplies`, pin its schema version and qualify a separate map; do not assume its array index is a durable physical identity.

Create a model-specific mapping table reviewed against the DMTF schema, vendor API guide, and BMC UI. Map Redfish State values conservatively: `Absent` can establish absent presence only for the represented slot; `Enabled` can establish enabled operation but does not by itself establish OK health; standby variants map to standby only after qualification. Keep Health separate from State. Derive redundancy only from the platform's explicit redundancy resource and membership, not from “two supplies observed.” Map standard Redfish `LineInputStatus` values `Normal`, `LossOfInput`, and `OutOfRange` directly to `normal`, `lost`, and `out_of_range`; null is not normal. Redfish failure or predictive-failure facets remain `unsupported` unless a separately documented standard or OEM property is qualified.

For IPMI, poll the current power-supply sensor state, not `sel list`. IPMI power-supply sensor type 0x08 defines discrete offsets for presence detected, failure detected, predictive failure, AC lost, AC lost/out-of-range, AC out-of-range while present, configuration errors, and inactive. Preserve the numeric sensor type, sensor number/record ID, supported-state mask, current asserted offsets, event-reading type, reading-unavailable/scanning flags, sensor name, entity, and FRU/slot association. Multiple offsets can be asserted simultaneously, so store a sorted native list and map each facet independently; never collapse the first matching string into one state. Only infer absence from a deasserted presence bit when the sensor declares that state supported and model qualification proves it represents the slot. A reading-unavailable response, disabled scan, unrecognized offset, missing SDR/FRU join, or ambiguous duplicate name makes the snapshot incomplete.

Set stable identity deliberately. `bmc_id` should be a governed asset UUID or management-controller inventory key, `chassis_id` a stable contained-chassis key, and `psu_id` a stable physical bay/location key within that chassis. Redfish `@odata.id` is useful native identity but may change after firmware; IPMI SDR record ID and display name can also reorder. Qualify location, member URI, entity/instance, and FRU evidence through replacement and firmware tests. `collector_instance` is a stable deployment/inventory identifier, not a random process UUID. Changing protocol, mapping contract, or collector ownership intentionally starts a new series and therefore has no inferred transition from the old series.

## Step 2 — Configure Splunk ingestion and source health

Emit one compact JSON line for every slot after the entire target poll succeeds. Recommended common fields are `contract_version=1`, stable identities, `collector_status`, `snapshot_complete`, integer `sample_epoch`, `source_protocol`, all canonical facets, `psu_name`, `native_resource`, `native_state`, `native_health`, and `native_active_states`. Emit a target-level error event when authentication, TLS, timeout, HTTP status, pagination, schema, IPMI command, SDR/FRU, or parsing fails. Do not emit last-known state with a fresh sample epoch. If atomic target snapshots are not possible, document per-member behavior and operate inventory completeness checks before interpreting silence.

Configure a five-minute scripted or modular input in `TA_power_supply_state`; a representative stanza is:

```ini
[script://$SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps/TA_power_supply_state/bin/collect_power_supply_state]
disabled = 0
interval = 300
index = hardware
source = power_supply_state_snapshot
sourcetype = hardware:power_supply:state
```

Splunk's interval is measured around script execution, so 300 seconds is a target cadence. Bound HTTP/IPMI timeouts below the interval, cap concurrency to the BMC vendor's supported rate, follow Redfish pagination, close sessions, and emit explicit errors. Expected successful volume is `inventoried PSU slots × 288` events per day; two slots across 1,000 servers produce about 576,000 compact events/day before errors. This is event arithmetic, not a licensing estimate; measure serialized bytes and index size on canaries.

Configure one-line JSON and event time on the applicable parsing/search tiers:

```ini
[hardware:power_supply:state]
SHOULD_LINEMERGE = false
LINE_BREAKER = ([\r\n]+)
TRUNCATE = 16384
TIME_PREFIX = "sample_epoch"\s*:\s*
TIME_FORMAT = %s
MAX_TIMESTAMP_LOOKAHEAD = 10
KV_MODE = json
```

Do not combine `KV_MODE=json` with `INDEXED_EXTRACTIONS=JSON` for the same source type; Splunk documents duplicate extraction in that configuration. Verify effective settings with `btool`, confirm `_time=sample_epoch`, inspect `_indextime-_time`, and ensure one event per expected slot and epoch. Build independent health searches for expected versus observed BMCs/slots, newest sample, status, incomplete snapshots, unsupported/unknown prevalence, exact duplicate keys, identity churn, protocol/map versions, and poll duration. An empty transition result is not proof that collection or current hardware state is healthy.

## Step 3 — Create and understand the transition search

Save the catalogue SPL as `power_supply_state_changes` and schedule it every five minutes after measuring ingestion lag. The base search reads from 17 minutes ago through two minutes ago. The final `sample_epoch` filter emits only the completed five-minute result bucket from seven through two minutes before dispatch, while the earlier data supplies prior-state history; schedule at minutes ending in 2 and 7 (or an equivalent five-minute cadence) so those boundaries align with poll buckets. Adjacent intervals from 120 through 900 seconds are accepted. Move both schedule windows based on measured lag, but do not expand the 900-second continuity rule without explicitly deciding that an unseen intermediate state can be ignored.

The first `where` is the contract firewall: schema, successful collection, complete snapshot, valid identity, protocol, epoch, and closed facet vocabularies are mandatory. `unknown` is absent from each allowed list. A facet may be `unsupported`, allowing heterogeneous hardware, but an unsupported-to-supported change is not a hardware transition. `stats count` groups the exact sample identity and rejects a count other than one; this prevents arbitrary ordering of duplicate events. Resolve duplicate collection instead of replacing the guard with `dedup`.

Ascending `sort` is mandatory. `streamstats current=f window=1 last(...)` attaches the immediately previous complete event in exactly the same host, contract, collector, protocol, BMC, chassis, and PSU series. The first event has no previous epoch and is removed by the interval gate. A changed identity or protocol begins a new series, and a gap over 900 seconds is intentionally not bridged. The eight comparison flags require both values to be supported and different. `changed_fields` is therefore an auditable list of canonical facets, not a free-text keyword hit.

Ranking is notification policy, not DMTF or IPMI terminology. Absent presence, critical health, lost input, asserted failure, lost redundancy, or operational absence receives rank 4; warning health, disabled/offline operation, out-of-range input, predictive failure, configuration mismatch, or degraded redundancy receives rank 3; standby receives rank 1. The maximum previous/current rank labels a transition degraded, recovered, or changed at equal rank. Recovery is `info`; degradation routes by current rank. The table retains every previous/current facet and raw native context. Tune routing only through a reviewed policy layer; never erase exact states or claim that rank 4 means physical irreparability.

Trigger when result count is greater than zero. Keep every dispatch result, and throttle notification only on exact PSU identity plus direction for a bounded period. A static failed PSU appears once when it enters failure; operate a separate latest-current-state search so unresolved critical states remain visible after the transition notification. Do not automatically issue Redfish actions, IPMI commands, chassis shutdowns, load transfers, ticket closure, or alarm acknowledgement from this alert.

## Step 4 — Validate identity, mappings, transitions, and gates

On each canary model, compare with the vendor UI by matching the same poll to the BMC hardware inventory/power-supply page. For Redfish, save the service-root traversal, PowerSubsystem, PowerSupply collection/member, and redundancy payloads; verify chassis/bay identity, Status.State, Status.Health, member links, and displayed redundancy. For IPMI, compare the qualified tool's current sensor detail, supported/current offsets, SDR entity and FRU/slot identity with the UI. Account for adjacent sampling time, but do not accept a different bay, unsupported-state assumption, or health/operational conflation.

Execute every positive and negative `controlTest` case with absolute time bounds. Inspect rows before and after `streamstats`. Prove that the prior event is from the same exact PSU, the 300-second interval is retained, two changed facets produce one row, degradation and recovery ranks are correct, and native wording alone does not trigger. Test exact interval boundaries: 120 and 900 seconds are accepted; 119 and 901 are rejected. Duplicate the same sample key and confirm both copies are rejected rather than forming a zero-second or arbitrary transition. Change each grouping key in turn and confirm no cross-boundary comparison.

Test every native mapping with normal, warning/failure, recovery, unsupported, unavailable, and unrecognized values. For IPMI, test simultaneous assertion bits and deassertion; for Redfish, test absent slot, standby/disabled variants, null Health, member disappearance, pagination, 401/403, timeout, and schema/OEM changes. A failed or partial poll must create source-health evidence and no fresh complete state. Perform an approved canary hot-swap or redundancy test only under the hardware/facilities procedure; capture before, degraded, and recovered snapshots plus same-time native UI/API/tool evidence.

Keep `status=draft` until controls have run in the target Splunk version, BMC models and firmware; TLS/authentication and secret handling have passed review; identity survives restart, firmware update, and PSU replacement; maps have hardware/vendor SME approval; and alert routing/runbooks have been exercised. This documentation review did not execute those gates.

## Step 5 — Operationalize response, evidence, and suppression

Put source-health and inventory tiles above transition and current-state panels. A responder should first confirm a fresh complete snapshot, exact physical bay, and authoritative collector. Then compare a new native read and BMC UI; inspect all changed facets and redundancy membership; check adjacent supplies, input feeds, chassis/system events, facilities telemetry, firmware/BMC resets, and approved maintenance; determine whether workload or service resilience changed; and consult model-specific service documentation before dispatch or replacement. Escalate input/redundancy loss to facilities and hardware owners even when PSU Health remains OK. Escalate physical intervention only to personnel authorized for electrical and hot-swap work.

Retain the artifacts listed in `evidence` under local operations/incident policy. BMC addresses, serials, topology, raw APIs, and credentials are sensitive; restrict collection config, raw events, dashboards, exports, and lookup changes by role. Apply only exact, expiring post-result suppression described in `knownFalsePositives`; retain suppressed rows and review recovery transitions. Never hide source-health failures or use a site-wide wildcard during maintenance.

## Step 6 — Troubleshoot without fabricating state

- **No events:** verify target inventory, app assignment, executable/runtime, secret access, route, DNS, TLS trust, effective input stanza, and scripted/modular-input logs. Query the service root or local IPMI interface with the collector identity; do not bypass TLS or grant administrator rights as a shortcut.
- **401/403 or session errors:** verify the Redfish session lifecycle, read role, account lockout, token expiry, clock, and vendor limits. Never index tokens or switch permanently to Basic authentication to hide session defects.
- **PowerSubsystem or PowerSupplies missing:** follow hyperlinks from the actual service root/chassis and inspect `@odata.type`. Determine whether the platform implements deprecated chassis `Power` or an OEM path. Add only a pinned, tested adapter; do not guess a URI from another vendor.
- **IPMI state is unavailable or empty:** inspect sensor event/reading type, supported assertion mask, scanning and reading-unavailable flags, SDR cache, FRU association, driver/transport, BMC reset, and tool version. Empty text is not `clear`.
- **JSON exists but fields are null:** inspect `_raw`, exact source type, `KV_MODE`, timestamp stanza, and extraction tier. The search rejects malformed contracts by design; fix parsing rather than adding `fillnull value=ok`.
- **Duplicate samples:** compare exact epoch, collector instance, deployment server, input stanza, scheduler overlap, replay/checkpoint behavior, and target ownership. Keep rejection until there is exactly one authoritative event.
- **No transition for a visible current fault:** find the prior complete sample. A first sighting, long data gap, protocol/contract/identity change, or fault predating the search horizon cannot prove a transition. Surface the current fault in the separate latest-state panel.
- **Unexpected transition after firmware or service:** compare stable location identity, Redfish URI, SDR/FRU records, serial/part data, map version, and native payload. Begin a new contract/identity series when semantics changed; do not join by display name alone.
- **Redundancy disagrees with member health:** preserve both. Group status can represent capacity/membership while each member reports OK. Verify explicit group mode, minimum needed, active/member links, and vendor UI; never infer full redundancy solely from member count.
- **Repeated recovery/degradation:** inspect input power, connector seating, BMC logs, facilities events, state hysteresis, poll timing, and raw snapshots. Do not suppress flapping until physical and mapping causes are investigated.

Requalify traversal, identities, maps, complete-snapshot behavior, controls, alert policy, and source-health checks after BMC/system firmware, hardware model, PSU/FRU, Redfish schema, IPMI tool/library, credential model, collector, parsing, or Splunk platform changes.
grandmaExplanation: We watch each server power unit and remember its last complete condition. When one unit changes—for example, it loses power, reports a fault, drops redundancy, or returns to normal—the team sees exactly what changed and which physical unit needs attention.
hardware: A server or chassis with a BMC exposing power-supply inventory and complete current state through DMTF Redfish PowerSupply/PowerSubsystem resources or an IPMI power-supply discrete sensor plus qualified SDR/FRU identity. Redfish is preferred for typed resource identity and status; IPMI requires exact sensor-state and identity qualification per platform.
